citations.assessment: The match is Mishnah Yoma 4:4, which names Menaḥem without a patronymic on the gold color, after Yose on the pan sizes. Bavli Yoma contains it on 43b. Correct the mistaken English locator. The Hebrew locator is preserved as printed.
The separate Vardimos entry explicitly reports the identity from this Bavli passage. It does not settle the distinct Yoma identification.
Shabbat expressly equates Menaḥem and Vardimos when listing Yose’s sons.
The exact formula is in Tosefta Bava Metzia in the house-and-upper-story case.

The precise occurrence of the full name in this checked Sifra transcription is under Emor on Leviticus 24:16. It parallels the Shevuot passage on explicit mention of the Name. Retain the inherited locator as printed pending edition comparison.
The named tannaitic rule about conflicting witnesses is found on 31b in the compared witness. Preserve the cited number and attach the link to the matched passage.
The Bavli explicitly attributes the baraita about cursing parents with the divine Name to Menaḥem bar Yose.
The received Tanḥuma recension explicitly gives Menaḥem bar Yose’s interpretation concerning lighting lamps in dark alleys.
The compared Bavli reads Yosef. Keep the witness name and Heilprin’s proposed replacement Yose as distinct readings.
Yoḥanan expressly assigns the attribution of the marketplace ruling to Menaḥem bar Yose Setimta’ah. Heilprin infers tannaitic standing.
The quoted form is Menaḥem Setimta’ah without a patronymic in the base Gemara.
The gloss describes why Menaḥem is styled Setimta’ah and does not give a patronymic there.
The exact Rashi gloss identifies Vardimos son of Yose with Menaḥem son of Yose and calls him the son of holy ones.
The next entry expressly contests the quoted Rashi gloss. It is a reference to Heilprin’s critique, with his closing judgment preserved as his own.

holds.raw: ויש דוחה זה דהול"ל ר' מנחם בנו
holds.reason: The relevant Mishnah names Menaḥem with no patronymic. Preserve Heilprin’s tentative identification and the separate objection as two readings of that sparse evidence.
The named attribution is unlocated on the cited folio or its other side. Shabbat 118b independently gives the full name and is already the relevant witness for Kol Kitvei.
